data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject when its guard clauses are enforced by a registry or installation step before the test can pass, and it describes its subject when the test reads back values that the subject's own construction already guarantees; the 3-of-26 result occurred because compile.py's shown-to-fail-first installation mutates the registry, and mutations that alter only declared data or add behavior are invisible to guards that check only the registry.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation changes a value that the guard does inspect, the test constrains the mutation by failing the installation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the registry is rebuilt after each mutation, the shown-to-fail-first installation may not produce the same distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the guard clauses are removed or bypassed, the test's constraining force disappears.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The test's constraining force comes from an external authority (the registry or installation guard) that must reject a mutation before the test can run. When a mutation changes behavior that the guard does not inspect, the test can only describe the behavior that remains unchanged.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
